cohort: The study will include women aged 16 to 49 years with recorded births in 2023, from 24 to 42 weeks' gestation in the United States, with a primary analysis potentially restricted to nulliparous women.
finding: The study hypothesizes that the risk of cesarean section will increase with an increase in maternal BMI category, and that BMI at birth may be a more relevant predictor of cesarean section than pre-pregnancy BMI.
mod_finding: The risk of cesarean section is hypothesized to increase with an increase in maternal BMI category, and BMI at birth may be a more relevant predictor of cesarean section than pre-pregnancy BMI.
